title: Radio: Stair Team 2, Pump Dead on the Floor 4–5 Landing with Bed 3-04

lines.text: ICU Charge, stair team 2. We're in the stairwell between floors 4 and 5 with Bed 3-04 in the stair chair. The pump just alarmed battery depleted and shut off. All three channels are stopped. Norepinephrine at 8 mics a minute, heparin at 1,200 units an hour, insulin at 4 units an hour.
Last MAP was 66 before we left the floor. Portable monitor now reads 58. He's awake, talking, but he's pale. We have no spare pump with us.
A nurse on 4 is at the landing door offering the L and D pump off their wall, but it's on the labor and delivery library. Do we take it or wait? Stair team 2, standing by.

fields.voiceStyle: Female ICU staff nurse, early 30s, breathless from the stairs, controlled but clearly worried; speaks fast and short; stairwell echo

instructorNote: Technical hurdle: watch for the ICU Charge to hold the team on the landing with one person watching the patient, turn down the L&D pump because the pump library is locked to the unit profile, send a charged ICU-profile pump from 6 West, restart norepinephrine first, then reconcile the 3 infusions and notify the provider about the MAP. The CNO should order a battery check on every pump before the next move (NUR-EM-07 step 3) and track whether the delay has to be disclosed within 60 minutes (NUR-EM-07 section 8).
